BiblicalUsage: marchesheth is a stewpan or frying pan, and it occurs twice, both times in the law of the meat offering. In Leviticus 2:7 an oblation baked in the frying pan shall be made of fine flour with oil, and in Leviticus 7:9 all that is dressed in the frying pan shall be the priest's that offers it. The word is the kitchen vessel of sacrifice.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marchesheth shows me that God cares about the vessels of His worship, and that the frying pan has its place in His law.
